Record.dc.html.title: The record — a panel, not a pop-up

nA.text:
A · WHO IS BLOCKING — the axis is OWNERSHIP

Five lanes are the shop's vocabulary, not the question. The question is who you would have to ring. So the board becomes one grouped list: waiting on you, waiting on a supplier, waiting on your own people. Six columns, 44px rows, eleven live orders on one screen without scrolling.

A band above it names the one thing holding the most money still, and carries the only red button on the page.

New here: a LEAVES column — can this make today's 15:00 run — and supplier batching, so two orders on one supplier are one message.

TRADEOFF: the board people already know is gone. Fastest to read, the most to unlearn.

nB.text:
B · LIST & RECORD — the axis is CONTINUITY  (my recommendation)

One order, one row, one place on the screen. Today an order can be in three places at once: the queue, "Behind it", and its lane. Here the strip is the filter, the list is sorted by who needs you, and the record opens in the right half instead of over the top — so six decisions get cleared without a dialog opening once.

Six stage cells replace four figures that were three zeros and a dash, and each says what its money IS: 1,120,000 to pay, 2,755,000 to pack, 88,000 to invoice.

TRADEOFF: the lanes become a filter, not a picture. You lose the shape of the pipeline at a glance and gain a screen you can work straight down.

nC.text:
C · THE BOARD, CORRECTED — the axis is FAMILIARITY

Every fault fixed, nothing moved. The five teaching sentences go behind the "i". A lane's own act becomes an icon. The queue stops printing a second copy of a card and rings the one it means, in the lane where it already sits. No cell on the strip is allowed to read zero.

The card is four lines now, because a 218px lane cannot hold "Ssekitoleko Hardware" and "2,150,000" on one — at three lines every second client name was cut.

TRADEOFF: look at the air. Eleven live orders and the board is still two-thirds empty, because a lane must be as tall as the busiest one. That is the board's ceiling, and it is the argument for B.

nR.text:
THE RECORD — what the pop-up becomes

Faults in the one that ships: it covers the lane you opened it from, so you cannot watch the order move. "Print packing list" is the most prominent button while the act you came for sits bottom-right. The stage rail says "not yet" four times. Two empty photo boxes spend 130px saying nothing was photographed. And "Margin 4.0%" is a percentage with nothing to measure it against.

So: a panel flush right, four lanes still readable behind it; the act above the reading rather than under 600px of it; three tabs for the lines, the history and the goods; and the margin measured against your 10% floor, with the price that would hold it.

nP.text:
THE PHONE — 820px is a switch, not a reflow

The split has no second column here, so the list is the screen and the record is a sheet. 15px body, 44px taps, and the one act inside the thumb's arc at the foot of the decision card.

The strip becomes 2x2 in a single card, hairline dividers, no tile borders. The stage filter becomes a scroller. The tab bar's active mark is FILLED, not tinted — a shape change reads at arm's length in daylight where a colour change does not.

Same eleven orders, same derivations, so the two screens can never say different things.
